pr_title: Delay progress bar in Copy-Item and Remove-Item cmdlets
pr_body:
<!-- Anything that looks like this is a comment and can't be seen after the Pull Request is created. -->

# PR Summary
I've optimized the Progress Bar of the Copy and Remove commands to display only after the operation lasts more then 200ms, otherwise do the operation without a Progress Bar, I've done this by adding to the IF conditional of IF _copyStopwatch or _removeStopwatch Elapsed time is higher then 0.2 seconds(200ms) add the Progress Bar to the process.

issue_context.title: `Remove-Item` progress should only be displayed if > 5 items
issue_context.body:
### Summary of the new feature / enhancement

https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/pull/20778 added progress for `remove-item`, but for small sets of items it can be a bit annoying to see it flash "removing 1" or 2 items.  I think it makes sense to not write progress unless the number of items is at least >5 and/or total time exceeds 2 seconds

### Proposed technical implementation details (optional)

_No response_
comments: Thank you @SteveL-MSFT for this issue. The Interactive Working group has reviewed this and agrees that displaying the progress bar for items that take less than a couple of seconds doesn't make sense. Rather than worry about the count of the number, we think we should be focused on the duration.

review_comments: `double speed = ...` should be moved under follow `if`.

1. This shouldn't be skipped while _removeStopwatch.Elapsed.TotalSeconds <= 0.2
2. I'd make 0.2 C# const since it is used twice.
3. I think 0.2 too small for interactive scenario. I believe user can wait 3-5 seconds before start worrying.

Am i understanding correctly, that you want me to make it so that instead of all of it being skipped, the calcuations continue while the instance of the progressBar is created only after 3 - 5 seconds elapsed?

Yes. 
We should do `_removedFiles++` while we don't show progress bar.
